q: Which statements about `private balance` versus `#balance` are true? Select all that apply.
options: Both make `acc.balance` / `acc.#balance` a compile error outside the class
`private` is erased with the other types, so `(acc as any).balance` still reads it at runtime
A `#balance` field is hidden by JavaScript itself, even from code that uses `any`
`private` makes the field read-only inside the class too
explain: Both are compile-time errors from outside. But `private` is a TypeScript type annotation, and types are erased, so at runtime it's an ordinary property that `any` can reach. `#` fields are a JavaScript feature, enforced when the code runs. Neither makes the field read-only: the class's own methods can change it freely. That's what `readonly` is for.

q: The checkout code from the lesson catches every error and shows "Card declined". What is the smallest change that stops a typo's `ReferenceError` from being reported as a declined card?
options: Check `if (err instanceof CardDeclinedError)` before showing the message, and `throw err` otherwise
Add a `finally` block that logs the error
Throw strings instead of `Error` objects so they're easier to compare
explain: Only handle the error you expect, and re-throw the rest so bugs crash loudly. `finally` runs for every outcome, so it can't tell errors apart. TypeScript doesn't allow annotating the catch variable with a specific class, because anything can be thrown, and even if it could, an annotation checks nothing at runtime. Strings lose the stack trace and can't be matched with `instanceof`.
